memory_candidates.content: For a binary with no --version/--help flag and no elan-toolchain path visible to ldd (e.g. lean4export in the Comparator toolchain), version-compatibility cannot be checked via binary introspection. A robust alternative: bounded (e.g. 5-level) directory walk-up from the resolved binary's realpath looking for a sibling marker file (here, lean-toolchain), diffed against the target's own copy of that marker. A 'no marker file found within the bound' outcome must be reported as an explicit UNKNOWN/cannot-verify state, never silently treated as a pass — this is easy to get wrong by defaulting to whichever branch is coded last.

When mirroring the same bash logic in two markdown files (a skill and its command wrapper), extract both to scratch files and diff them byte-for-byte as a verification step. Byte-identical blocks are strong, cheap evidence of zero drift between the two authored copies — cheaper than manually re-reading both for consistency.
